{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./array_job.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from PBS:
#   -l select=1:ncpus=24   -> -N 1 -n 1 -c 24
#   -l walltime=1:00:00    -> -t 1h
#   -J 1-21:21             -> one array element (index 1) with step size 21 (i.e., processes 1..21)
#                             (implemented by passing an index into the payload)

# NOTE: PBS -P CBBI1106 not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: accounting/charging may not be applied as intended; some sites require project/account specified out-of-band.

# NOTE: PBS -q smp not translated.
# Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the smp queue.

# NOTE: PBS -o/-e paths not translated.
# Performance implication: none; operational implication: stdout/stderr will follow Flux defaults unless configured at submission.

# NOTE: PBS -M/-m (email notifications) not translated.
# Performance implication: none; operational implication: no email notifications.

# Since the PBS array specification here expands to a single chunk, submit exactly one Flux job.
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 24 -t 1h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner 1")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  PBS_ARRAY_INDEX=${2:-1}

  sleep 4

  module add chpc/R/3.5.1-gcc7.2.0

  cd /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/ || exit 1

  make sbv

  STEP=21
  START=$PBS_ARRAY_INDEX
  END=$(( START + STEP - 1 ))

  for i in $(eval echo "{$START..$END}")
  do
    (echo "process $i started" && Rscript sbv/method_1_analysis/method_1_arrayjob.R "$i" && echo "process $i finished") &
  done

  sleep 0.1
  echo "Waiting for processes to finish"
  wait $(jobs -p)
  echo "All processes finished"
fi
"
}
